### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c40506aac02df70aad25588a19a629fa2efa4c62` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2514e030e701846da084c9a64e1198044998475f` — the merge of head `cf5965828a810054ea69caad37f17e7e6993e42d` into base `c40506aac02df70aad25588a19a629fa2efa4c62`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2514e030e701846da084c9a64e1198044998475f && git checkout 2514e030e701846da084c9a64e1198044998475f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c40506aac02df70aad25588a19a629fa2efa4c62 cf5965828a810054ea69caad37f17e7e6993e42d && git checkout -B drift-repro c40506aac02df70aad25588a19a629fa2efa4c62 && git merge --no-ff cf5965828a810054ea69caad37f17e7e6993e42d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c40506aac02df70aad25588a19a629fa2efa4c62
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf5965828a810054ea69caad37f17e7e6993e42d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.ts, packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/public-form-required.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`isMultiValueField`, `ValueShapeFieldDef` :361-375), packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts (`validationFailure` :76), packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (the flat `VALIDATION_FAILED` arm :1183-1192, `armSentence` :310), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (`mapDataError`), packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts (`renderValidationMessage` :358, catalog `required` :99), packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (form entry `required` / `hidden` :3439-3440, entry `visibleWhen` :3552, section `visibleWhen` :3837), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`readFormObjectDefinitions`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:2864, packages/spec/liveness/view.json (the `sections` row), the three `package.json` dependency edges and `.` entries of core / objectql / rest, `.changeset/config.json` + `.changeset/pre.json`, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs (LEDGER), the WHICH LEVEL ruling in .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml :754. The three `.changeset/24131-*.md` are read for ② only; `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx` is a prose face and is the dispatching seat's ACCEPT, not judged here. No non-prose path of the diff is left to the lane seat.

Inputs: card #24131 (body and all six comments, rulings 6229368836 / 6230121735 / 6230321666 and the three `os-dev-report`s included), PR #24161 (body, 10-file list, net diff of `6dede7a51...cf5965828`, 4 commits, +509/−24), and the 47 check-runs on the head. Read-only: no checkout, build, test or gate run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`@objectstack/core` `.` entry WIDENS by two exports — RIGHT.** `packages/core/src/index.ts` adds `export * from './utils/required-emptiness.js'`; the new module exports `isMissing(value)` and `isEmptyForRequired(def, value)`, typed on `@objectstack/spec/data`'s `ValueShapeFieldDef` (`{ type: string; multiple?: boolean; options? }`). Both bodies are byte-identical to the private copies deleted from `record-validator.ts` (`v === undefined || v === null || (typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() === '')`; then `isMultiValueField(def) && Array.isArray(value) && value.length === 0`). core already depends on `@objectstack/spec` at runtime and `isMultiValueField` is reachable through the addressable `./data` export; core's `.` entry maps to `dist/index.*`, so the two symbols are published. No api-surface baseline covers core, so nothing owes a regeneration. The core pin reads both through `../index.js`, the `.` entry both consumers import.

2. **`@objectstack/objectql`: NO public-surface change; published bytes change — RIGHT.** The record validator's five read sites at the head (`:760` blank-to-null normalisation, `:1026` the insert `required` arm, `:1029` the early return, `:1745` the value-shape scan, `:2007` the PATCH `required_cleared` arm) now call the imports from `@objectstack/core`; the private copies are gone and nothing else in the file defines or calls them. objectql's own `FieldDef` (`type: string`, `multiple?: boolean`) satisfies `ValueShapeFieldDef` structurally, so the call sites are unchanged in meaning. The `autonumber` skip stays at the engine's arm, where the core module's docblock says it belongs. Nothing exported by objectql is renamed, retired or re-typed.

3. **`POST /forms/:slug/submit` NARROWS its accept set — RIGHT, and the narrowing is exactly the card's route (a).** On the head, the allow-list loop (`form-routes.ts` :437-455) collects, off the same `sections[].fields` entries, every object entry with `required === true` that is not `hidden: true`, carries no `visibleWhen`, and sits in a section with no `visibleWhen` (string entries carry no `required`, so they are never judged). After the allow-list filter and the anchor / prototype-key strip, and before `createData` (:556-589), each such field minus the server-managed anchors and the three prototype keys is judged on `filteredData` — what the door writes — with `isEmptyForRequired(objectFieldDef, value)` (the object definition read through `readFormObjectDefinitions`, whose `fields` is a map keyed by name, the same shape the resolve route reads at :369). An empty value throws `validationFailure(messages joined by '; ', entries)`, and the route's catch maps it through `mapDataError(error)` to the flat arm at `data-error-classification.ts:1183`: `400`, top-level `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `error` = the thrown message, `fields[]` of `{ field, code: 'required', message, label }`, and no `object` key, because the catch passes none — the same arm, the same keys and the same absence the engine's object-level refusal gets on this route. No error code is minted. Nothing refused before is accepted now: the new block only throws, and the allow-list, the `[#3022]` anchor strip, the `[#6920]` zero-sections refusal and the `createData` call are untouched. The refusal happens before any write, so no row is stored; the pins assert the row count.
   - **The judged set is narrower than "every form-required entry" — RIGHT as a boundary, declared on every prose face.** `hidden: true` entries, entries with a `visibleWhen`, and entries in a section with a `visibleWhen` are not judged. The spec's own describe text on both keys (view.zod.ts :3552 and :3837) says nothing server-side evaluates a form-view `visibleWhen`, so the server cannot know whether the visitor was shown the field; judging unconditionally would refuse what the visitor never saw. The residual is fail-OPEN, and it should be read as such: a `required: true` entry gated by a predicate stays unenforced on this door exactly as before, including the `current_user` predicates that fault open on the public route and show the field to everyone. That is the lenient direction — the door refuses nothing it did not declare — and the PR body, the rest changeset and the docs sentence all state it.
   - **Message and label chain — RIGHT, with one stated residual.** The route renders through `renderValidationMessage({ messageKey: 'required', label, field, params: {} })`, the catalog entry `'{{label}} is required'`, and takes the label as `def.label.trim()` else the field name — the same tail `resolveFieldLabel` (:432-433) ends in. The one step the route omits is the engine's i18n `translate` lookup, which runs only when the execution context carries `translate`, `objectName` AND `locale`; the anonymous submit context (`publicFormGrant`, `permissions`, `anonymous`) carries no locale, so on this route the engine renders the default locale too, and the pins assert both levels answer the same words. Residual: a context that one day carries a locale would localise the engine's refusal and not the route's — noted in ③.
   - **The object-definition fallback — acceptable.** When the object definition or its field `type` is unreadable the route judges with `isMissing` alone, dropping the `[]` arm. That state is degenerate (an insert on an object with no definition fails downstream anyway), and the fallback errs toward accepting, never toward refusing.
   - **Cost, not contract:** a submit with at least one judged field now performs one `getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })` read before the write, the same read the resolve route already performs per request.
   - **A field both levels require** is refused by the route first, with the exact body the engine answered before (pinned verbatim against the pre-fix measurement); a field only the object requires is still refused by the engine, unchanged. No visible change for either cell.

4. **The pins cover the narrowing's whole accept-set edge.** `public-form-required.test.ts` drives the real route through `RestServer` → protocol → `ObjectQL` → `SqlDriver` sqlite with only `getMetaItems` stubbed: absent / `null` / `''` / whitespace on a form-required text field, `[]` / absent on a form-required `tags` field, two missing fields named together in form order, the `201` control that stores the row as sent, the engine's unchanged object-level refusal with key-for-key envelope equality, the both-levels verbatim body, and the hidden / conditional-entry / conditional-section boundary at `201`. The core pin covers each arm of the rule beside a present twin, including `[]` on `json` (not empty) and on a single-valued lookup (not empty). The dev reports one ablation on the `throw` line (8 of 11 red, the control and boundary and both-levels cells green, as predicted); that is the dev's report, not a verdict of this record.

5. **Check-runs on the head (47): 34 success, 7 skipped, 6 in_progress.** Every derived gate family that answers a contract question is green: `Check Changeset` (×2), `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, the card/branch claim guards. **Pending at read time: `Test Core (1/6)` through `Test Core (6/6)`** — the unit-suite shards; not waited on. The landing precondition "every check green" is the owning seat's to confirm before the queue; this record's verdict is on the contract. No governed path is in the file list, so no Tier H word is owed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the PR body's line-initial declaration, the closed set's spelling for a diff that widens one surface (core's `.` entry) and narrows another (the submit door), and both facts are true of this diff.

- **`@objectstack/core` `minor`, changeset `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — RIGHT.** Two new exports from a published `.` entry is the additive widening the WHICH LEVEL ruling grades at least `minor`.
- **`@objectstack/objectql` `patch`, changeset `Clause-②: no` — RIGHT.** No public-surface change; the published `dist` bytes change (the dev measured `function isEmptyForRequired` 1→0 in `dist/index.js` and `dist/core.js`), so `patch`, never none.
- **`@objectstack/rest` `patch`, changeset `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, summary `fix(rest)!:`, a visible `**BREAKING —` bullet, and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …` marker comment — RIGHT.** The marker is in the gate's grammar and the category is one of its `CATEGORIES`; the body carries no FROM → TO rewrite, arrow or table (the one sentence "the fix is to send that field" is a caller's payload, not a consumer-code or metadata rewrite), so the `no-migration-prescription` precondition holds statement-against-statement. On the level: rest's export surface is unchanged, and the WHICH LEVEL ruling (pr-automation.yml :754) says a `fix(` that changes no public surface stays `patch` and that during the launch window breaking-ness is carried by the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level — the rest changeset carries both carriers. `check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis on the body's `yes (narrowing)` reaches `discharged` (core's `minor` accounts for the declared axis; rest and objectql at `patch` are a reading set aside, printed, exit 0), and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. All three packages sit in the one fixed group in `pre` mode tag `next`, so the release version is lockstep whatever rest's own line says. `no (narrowing)` is the truthful per-package answer (rest widens nothing) and carries the arm the ADR-0087 gate reads; `no (widening)` appears nowhere.
- `skip-changeset` does not apply: three released packages publish.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag (reports 6230265113, 6231149249, 6231292769 and the PR's Acceptance notes) and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

1. **Judged set narrower than every form-required entry (hidden / `visibleWhen` / anchors)** — ANSWERED in ①.3: right, fail-open, declared on all three prose faces.
2. **Placement of the one emptiness predicate (report 1's `open_questions`, options A–D)** — ANSWERED by the seat's inherited ruling 6230321666 (core, as #23982's 6227928430), and the diff executes it: no `packages/spec` path moves, rest imports core (a declared runtime dependency, so no `check-undeclared-dep-imports` LEDGER row is owed; the LEDGER's only rest row stays the rest-server.ts optional engine probe), and objectql deletes its copies.
3. **`Clause-②` spelling (report 2's `open_questions`, A keep `yes` / B re-declare `yes (narrowing)`)** — ANSWERED: B was taken in patch round 1; the PR body reads `yes (narrowing)` line-initial, the per-package arms are as judged in ②, and the Acceptance-notes bullet the dev called stale now reads the post-patch state (checked against the body as served).
4. **Rest changeset at `no (narrowing)` rather than `yes (narrowing)`; the added `!` and BREAKING bullet** — ANSWERED in ②: right, and the banner is the ruling's named carrier.
5. **Label language / locale** — ANSWERED in ①.3 with the residual: the route's refusal never takes the engine's i18n `translate` step; equal on this route because the anonymous context carries no `locale`. If a later change gives the anonymous context a locale, the two doors' wording diverges — the seat that does so owes a pin.
6. **Liveness ledger `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, row `sections`** — ESCALATED to the spec seat (dispatch hold-off): the row's blanket `live` verdict over the FormField subtree names the submit route only for `allowedFields` ("submit builds allowedFields from them"); with this head the route also reads each entry's `required`, so the evidence owes that read point. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head, so nothing reds; a follow-up on the card's spec half, carrier to be set by the dispatching seat.
7. **`rule-validator.ts:2864` keeps a byte-identical private `isMissing`** (confirmed at the head) and **`screen-input-contract.ts` `isPresent`** — ESCALATED as drift candidates, no carrier; both outside this card's hold-offs; neither changes any accept set here.
8. **New boundary: a form entry declaring a `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` field `required: true`** — ESCALATED to the lint/spec lane. The resolve route strips those types from the anonymous rendering unconditionally (form-routes.ts :369-375, ruling E on #21079), so such an entry can never be filled from the page, and the submit now refuses it by name rather than storing the row without it. Refusing loudly is the right direction for a declared constraint (AGENTS.md's warn-vs-error rule; silently dropping a declared `required` is the trap this card is about); the authoring-time refusal of such an entry on an anonymous form is a lint rule, not this route's. The dev read no producer in the tree declaring one; no carrier yet — the dispatching seat files it.
9. **Docs sentence added though the page was silent** — a prose face, the dispatching seat's ACCEPT; no objection from this face: the sentence states the judged set and the exemptions exactly as the code does.
10. **`origin/main` moved `6dede7a51` → `c40506aac` during the run; branch not re-merged** — the 47 check-runs are on the PR's merge ref against current `main`, which is the verdict that counts; none of the four intervening commits is in core / objectql / rest per the dev's gate re-derivation, and the type-check and lint families are green on the head.
11. **Pending CI** — `Test Core (1/6)`–`(6/6)` in_progress at read time (①.5). Not waited on; the owning seat confirms green before the queue.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:cli` seat 1 · `os-sales` · session `session_01BVm1pAXVXQ3PjC42j1kPFf` · 2026-10-17T07:52Z

Head `cf5965828`. This is the seat's review of record for #24131 (claim `6230121735`, re-declared `6230321666`). The contract faces are judged by the at-tier record `6231404578` on this head (`Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, **PASS**, an isolated read-only agent fed the card, the PR and the check-runs only). This record covers what that one leaves to the seat: the form, the prose faces, the seat's own reading of the diff, and the landing.

- **Form:** draft → `main`; title `fix(rest, core)!: …`. The first line is `Fixes #24131`, the body's only closing keyword (scanned). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is line-initial and matches the claim's `yes`, with the arm the two-faced diff owes.
- **The ruling executed as ruled:** the required-emptiness predicate lives in `@objectstack/core` (`utils/required-emptiness.ts`, exported from `.`), as the inherited ruling `6227928430` homes a shared function. objectql's private copies are gone, rest imports core (a declared runtime dependency), and no `packages/spec` path moves (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 2).

  - `form-routes.ts` judges `required` off the same `sections[].fields` entries the allow-list reads, on what the route writes (`filteredData`, so a default or hook stamp cannot satisfy an omitted field), before the write.
  - It throws `validationFailure(...)`, so the catch's `mapDataError` answers the flat `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` the object-level refusal answers on this route.
  - The predicate bodies in `required-emptiness.ts` are byte-identical to the ones `record-validator.ts` deletes.
- **Prose faces, sentence by sentence against the diff:**
  - The rest changeset: "absent, `null`, `''`, only whitespace, or `[]` on a multi-value field is refused, and no row is created" matches the predicate arms, and the pins cover each arm with the row count unchanged. ✓ "An entry the form hides … or shows only conditionally … is not judged" matches the `hidden` / `visibleWhen` / section-`visibleWhen` conditions in the loop. ✓ "A server-managed anchor … is never judged" matches the `PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS` filter. ✓ "An object `defaultValue` or a `beforeInsert` hook does not satisfy a field the visitor omitted" holds because the route judges `filteredData`. ✓

  - `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`: the one added sentence states the judged set and the exemptions exactly as the loop does. ✓
- **The review's escalations, routed:**
  - Item 6, the `view.json` `sections` liveness row's evidence: a pointer to the `domain:spec` seat, posted on its seat post (one comment carries it; no card).
  - Item 7, the private emptiness copies in `rule-validator.ts:2864` and `screen-input-contract.ts`: Acceptance notes, no carrier. No reach was measured, so they are below the filing gate.

No producer in the tree and no door reading, so it is below the filing gate; its remedy is a new lint rule, which the four-axis framework defaults to "no" without a maintainer's naming. The route's loud refusal is the right direction meanwhile.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 24161`: 539 changed lines ≤ 3000). At this record, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are success on the head, and three `Test Core` shards are still running.
